title: User-Space Virtual File System Emulation
pattern: Simulating folders, permissions, and directory structures entirely inside the application's memory when native file systems are available.
why_bad: It ignores the highly optimized caching, file indexing, and permission boundaries provided natively by the operating system kernel. It duplicates file management bugs and increases memory usage.
detection: The presence of string-keyed tree structures representing files and folder paths parsed at runtime, rather than utilizing OS standard directories.
counterexample: **Unit Testing Fakes:** Simulating a file target for unit tests that run in memory without touching real disks.
source: [Robert C. Martin Series] Robert C. Martin - _Clean Architecture_ A Craftsman’s Guide to Software Structure and Design_ (2017, Prentice Hall).pdf, Chapter 17.
